openai.title: OpenAI — A practical guide to building agents

anthropic_tools.title: Anthropic — Tool use (incl. tool search for large tool sets)

principles: Start with the simplest design that meets the requirements; add steps or autonomy only when measurement shows the need.
Prefer predictable workflows over autonomous agents when the steps are known in advance.
Put guardrails and a human in the loop before irreversible or high-impact actions.
Ground answers in your data (RAG or long context) rather than the model's memory when facts matter.
Keep an evaluation set and re-run it before every prompt or model change.
Keep one agent until tool overload or clearly separate domains justify splitting it; route distinct request types before reaching for autonomy.

single_call.name: Single model call
single_call.what: One well-prompted call with structured output.
single_call.pick_if: one model is accurate enough and the task is a single step.

cascade.name: Small model first, escalate when unsure
flow: Large LLM only when the small one is under 80% sure
cascade.what: A cheap model answers first with a confidence score. Under 80% confidence, a stronger model answers instead.
cascade.pick_if: most requests are easy and cost or speed matter, but hard cases need a big model.
components: Confidence score in the output schema
Escalation threshold tuned on the eval set

decision_model.name: Decision model with LLM fallback
flow: LLM only when Jev is under 80% sure
decision_model.what: Jev picks the answer and says how sure it is. When it's under 80% sure, the request goes to an LLM instead.
decision_model.pick_if: the answer is one of a fixed set of labels, at high volume or low latency.

long_context.name: Whole documents in the prompt
long_context.what: Send the documents with each request; answer only from them. No index to build.
long_context.pick_if: documents are small (under ~100 pages) and change rarely.
components: Prompt caching for the document block
"Answer only from the text, else unknown" instruction

rag.name: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
rag.what: Retrieve the relevant passages, then answer only from them or say it doesn't know.
rag.pick_if: answers must come from large or changing documents.
components: Vector index (OpenSearch Serverless or Aurora pgvector)
Hybrid keyword + vector search with reranking

rag_cascade.name: RAG with small-to-large escalation
flow: Large LLM only when the small one is under 80% sure
rag_cascade.what: Retrieve the relevant passages, let a cheap model answer from them, and send only low-confidence answers to a stronger model.
rag_cascade.pick_if: answers come from your documents and most questions are simple lookups, so paying for the big model on every request is wasteful.
components: Vector index (OpenSearch Serverless or Aurora pgvector)
Confidence score in the output schema
Escalation threshold tuned on the eval set

workflow.name: Fixed workflow (prompt chain)
workflow.what: Steps defined in code — route the request, run a tested handler, verify — each a focused model call.
workflow.pick_if: the steps are known in advance and you want control and testability.

evaluator_optimizer.name: Draft, critique and revise
evaluator_optimizer.what: One call drafts, another checks it against clear criteria, and the draft is revised once.
evaluator_optimizer.pick_if: written quality matters and you can state what 'good' looks like.
components: Max one or two revision rounds

tool_agent.name: Tool-using agent
tool_agent.what: The model chooses which of your tools to call, in a loop, until the task is done.
tool_agent.pick_if: it must act in your systems and the steps vary per request.

multi_agent.name: Orchestrator with specialist agents
multi_agent.what: A lead model splits the task, workers research in parallel, the lead combines results.
multi_agent.pick_if: tasks are broad and open-ended and quality beats cost.
components: Budget and step caps per run

batch.name: Batch pipeline
batch.what: Collect requests and run them through the providers' batch APIs at about half price.
batch.pick_if: nobody waits for the answer (nightly jobs, backfills).

router.name: Router to specialised handlers
router.what: A small model sorts each request into a type; each type has its own tested prompt, tools and model.
router.pick_if: requests fall into a few distinct types that need different handling or different models.
components: Router with a fixed list of request types

agentic_rag.name: Agentic retrieval (search, read, search again)
agentic_rag.what: The model decides what to search, reads the results and searches again until it can answer, citing passages.
agentic_rag.pick_if: answers need several documents or sources combined, or a follow-up search after the first.
